_doc: Round 5 paint-over for q at 144 (r5_paint.py). Seeded from round 4's head layers (art/rosace/overrides/drive9/q_144.json) moved by the head-skin offset R4u -> R5xu (0, -2), then re-authored for the round-4 critics' face and hair fixes. Layers with port: true are also painted on the twin build (R5u).

layers.name: face_base
layers.why: Face critic 2: a clean face plane before the features (FC-P35); the old stamp's eyes are cleared.

layers.name: chin
layers.why: Face 2 (Q): 'a grey sleeve or shoulder mass sits right under the chin and cuts off the jaw ... a clear jaw and chin'. The sleeve cut the face flat at the mouth row; the jaw is drawn on over it as a tapering V to a 6 px chin with a warm dark underside (J), so the face ends in a chin, not a sleeve edge.

layers.name: brows
layers.why: Q: set brows angled toward the nose (determined, not startled).

layers.name: eye_far
layers.why: Face critic (round 4, face 2): 'narrow, slanted almond eyes with a heavy 2-3 px dark upper-lash block, a dark-to-warm iris ramp and a small catchlight; make it about 1 px narrower and tilted up at the outer corner, a 2 px near-black upper-lash block running 1 px past the outer corner, an iris of deep indigo on top, desaturated blue in the middle and a 1 px pale lower catchlight; drop the pure cyan; lift the lid 1 px'. Q (face 2, consistency): 'both eyes on one tilt line ... the far eye crowds the hairline'. Moved 2 px down and 1 px in from the hairline; the pair now rises 1 px over 9 px.

layers.name: blush
layers.why: Attractiveness 3 (round 4): 'lock one signature expression (half-lidded smirk, one brow slightly raised) and carry it into the back and Q frames; never ship an open O mouth in a key pose'; face 2: 'the default mouth is a 2-3 px asymmetric smirk; blush as 1-2 px strokes under the eye, not a blob'.

layers.name: mouth
layers.why: Face 2 (Q): 'replace the startled O mouth with a closed smirk (1-2 px)'. A 3 px closed line, the near corner lifted.

layers.name: strands_out
layers.why: Head and hair 4: a strand flung off the outline by the stamp.
